Traditional code review (including most AI review tools) operates in an isolated, static scope—it checks whether a diff is locally self-consistent but cannot answer "will merging this PR drag down the SLA of downstream services." Code simulation shifts the object of evaluation from "code text" to "the behavior trajectory of code in the real system": tracking how data flows propagate across services, predicting how state transitions, and exposing integration risks invisible to static analysis. The essence of this shift is moving quality assessment from syntactic correctness to runtime behavioral correctness.
